steps.content: The Gate of Hell is broken. Behind the shattered obsidian is a silent and pure white world. It's completely different from the twisted and treacherous world outside.
The winding staircase is covered with white films, and the distant wall is covered with pure white plaster statues. They look unfinished but contain a certain rough tension.
The mutation of fear seems to have not yet invaded the place.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Welcome to the special section of the Witching Hour, the <color=#fb9259>Unfinished Land</color>.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: It's mostly works I haven't finished or am not really satisfied with. But the museum likes them and set up this section.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...It's like the navigator has become alive. They have exactly the same voice, and it's making me really uncomfortable.
Hella mutters. She then tugs the corner of your clothes and whispers in your ear.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Hey, who's this woman? She was looking really weird when she was with you just now... Something must have happened while I was not with you. Are you two super close now?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She created all the works here and can destroy them. She can help... probably.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Hmph... A fancy artist? She seems pretentious and not very trustworthy. Are all Eastsiders like this?
Lisa glares at Hella.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Hehe, creators can lie, but their works can't. My works speak my heart.

options: Where is the owner of Witching Hour?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Right down here.
You descend slowly down the winding staircase. Looking down from the handrail, a statue of a holy woman stands in the center of the bottom.
Her hair looks vivid, and a veil half-covers her face. It's truly a beautiful masterpiece.
But the whiteness without temperature or sound doesn't give you a sense of tranquility. It reminds you of death and something frightening.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She doesn't look like the oddly shaped things out there.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Yes, this is her original look. She hasn't been distorted by Witching Hour yet.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: It's not finished, but she has gained far greater power than me.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Two months ago, I received a particular piece of stone. It was unmarked, and flawless, too perfect to be of this world. It has a mesmerizing power before I even start carving it.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: And the moment I touched it, an unprecedented inspiration struck me. All the fears I've ever experienced were spread out before my eyes. I heard people's struggles, and they were crying out the same name.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: ...<color=#fb9259>Sosia</color>. Her name is <color=#fb9259>Sosia</color>.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: I don't remember how I picked up my chisel and hammer, and every second of carving it was like an eternity. When I snapped out of it, the statue was already taking shape, as if it had been in the stone all along, waiting for me to awaken it.
Turning fear into reality... it's the same as Witching Hour's mutation. So is this stone the source of the problem?

options: Where did the stone come from?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: I couldn't trace it. We only found an anonymous letter in the shipping container.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: The person claimed to be my supporter. He asked me to carve the perfect piece out of this stone, portray my heart, and present it during Witching Hour.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: But I've seen a strange pattern.
Enfer draws an eye on the film on the side, and it's a pattern you're familiar with.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: It came to me in my dream one night while working on Sosia.
...It's the pattern of that man, Parma.
A piece of stone able to turn human emotions into reality, an anonymous giver… The last time, they extracted <color=#fb9259>joy</color>, and this time, it's pure <color=#fb9259>fear</color>.
It's still an intense emotion, but there's no <color=#fb9259>Corpus</color>. At least now, there's no risk of a Black Ring outbreak.
It's worth the trip to have got so much out of an unexpected crisis. All you have to do is to end this mutation before it causes more trouble.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Okay, okay, stop frowning, or you'll get wrinkles. Anyway, we have found the target. Smash that Sosia, and everything will be fine. We still have time for a Hallowing party.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Well, with the great artist here, it will be easy, right? Smashy smash, like she did just now? Right?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: ...Of course. I made a deal with your Chief to help you guys. And I want this long night to end too.
Do you really think so?
A low voice speaks. You look back to see Lisa, who has been silent for a long time.

steps.speaker: Lisa
steps.content: I've heard the name, Sosia. You were interviewed by <color=#fb9259>DisArt</color> and said it was your life's work. You wanted her to be a true masterpiece and realize your artistic vision.

steps.speaker: Lisa
steps.content: It seems pretty easy for you to ditch your masterpiece and dream, Enfer.

steps.speaker: Lisa
steps.content: Like with the Gate of Hell. You said it's your proud piece but didn't even blink when you destroyed it.

steps.speaker: Lisa
steps.content: Is the so-called thriller art just to attract attention? Eastside's art business must be so rotten if it's celebrating a deceitful person like you.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: Lisa, we have to destroy that statue to stop the mutation. That's the mission. Don't get emotional.

steps.speaker: Lisa
steps.content: You don't have to tell me. I know what I'm doing, and my question was for that woman who calls herself an artist!

steps.speaker: Lisa
steps.content: She said she wanted to be honest with her works, saying they held her dreams and ideals. If even those were lies, then aren't we the greatest fools for believing her?
The tension stops everyone in their tracks as Lisa glares at Enfer. She's always been sharp with her words, but you rarely see her so angry.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Lisa, right? A famous art critic who's sharp and straightforward. Do you like my works?

steps.speaker: Lisa
steps.content: ...Don't think of me as one of those people worshipping you in art salons.
Lisa's tone is strong, but she's not speaking as loud. Enfer laughs.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: I would never lie to my works. As an artist, I use the limited and trivial life of mine to create my own unique masterpieces. I put all my heart and soul into it every time I carve, dreaming of its birth.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: ...But it's not a world that one can enter easily.
With that, she swings her carving hammer and smashes a quietly approaching statue monster.

steps.speaker: Labyrinth
steps.content: Warning. A large number of enemies are coming suddenly. And they all have physical forms. Are they... Enfer's works?
The dark mist surrounding you suddenly stirs, and amidst the chaos, comical and ugly statues close in. Their maniacal laughter and screams encircle the stairs.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Ridiculous, isn't it? No matter what kind of great artworks I create, the audience's imagination of fear will twist it and cover it like layers and layers of plaster. And they all end up in weird shapes like this.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: This is not what I want to express at all. My "art" is not even close.
Enfer looks around at the crazed "art pieces," and there's no longer a smile on her face.
